islands.name: Booby Cay
islands.note: Boobies nest on bare cays and stare at sailors; on Bahamian charts many times over

islands.name: Îlet aux Fous
islands.note: French: islet of the boobies (fou, 'fool', is the French name for the bird)

islands.name: Staniel Rock
islands.note: Staniel: the old word for a kestrel, as in Staniel Cay in the Exumas

islands.name: Petrel Holm
islands.note: Petrels wail at night from their burrows

islands.name: Isle of Devils
islands.note: Spanish sailors' name for Bermuda, after the night shrieks of its nesting petrels

islands.name: Shrieking Isle
islands.note: Seabirds calling in the dark, taken for spirits

islands.name: Laughing Gull Cay
islands.note: After Belize's Laughing Bird Caye, named for the gulls that bred there

islands.name: Gannet Stack
islands.note: A stack whitened by nesting gannets

islands.name: Solan Stack
islands.note: Solan goose: the old seamen's name for the gannet

islands.name: Grog-Grog Rock
islands.note: Smyth's Sailor's Word-Book (1867): grog-grog, the soft cry of the solan goose

islands.name: Shag Rock
islands.note: Shags, the sea cormorants, dry their wings on it

islands.name: Mother Carey's Rock
islands.note: Storm petrels, 'Mother Carey's chickens', were said to foretell a gale

islands.name: Albatross Rock
islands.note: Albatrosses were thought to carry the souls of drowned sailors

islands.name: Pelican Cay
islands.note: A cay name wherever pelicans fish

islands.name: Man-o'-War Cay
islands.note: Man-o'-war bird: the sailors' name for the frigatebird

islands.name: Frigatebird Island
islands.note: Frigatebirds roost in its trees, red throats puffed

islands.name: Curlew Holm
islands.note: Cook named a Curlew Island in Dusky Sound, 1773

islands.name: Puffin Holm
islands.note: A grassy holm riddled with puffin burrows

islands.name: Tern Cay
islands.note: Terns nest on the bare sand

islands.name: Noddy Cay
islands.note: Noddies: tropical terns so tame that sailors thought them foolish

islands.name: Parrot Cay
islands.note: After the Parrot Cays of Abaco, home of the Bahama parrot

islands.name: Pigeon Cay
islands.note: One of the commonest names on Bahamian charts

islands.name: Egg Island
islands.note: Sailors landed to gather seabird and turtle eggs; Eleuthera has one

islands.name: Hummingbird Cay
islands.note: As in the Exuma Cays

islands.name: Raven Rock
islands.note: A black rock where ravens sit

islands.name: Hawksbill Cay
islands.note: After the hawksbill turtle, whose shell was the period's tortoiseshell

islands.name: Turtle Cay
islands.note: Green turtles come ashore to lay; Bahamian cays were named for them

islands.name: Loggerhead Key
islands.note: Loggerhead turtles nest here; Key is the older spelling of cay

islands.name: Sea Wolf Rocks
islands.note: Spanish sailors called the Caribbean monk seal the sea wolf, hence Cay Lobos

islands.name: Seal Holm
islands.note: Seals haul out on its ledges

islands.name: Selkie Skerry
islands.note: Orkney selkies: seals that shed their skins and walk ashore as people

islands.name: Whaleback Island
islands.note: A long, low ridge like a whale's back breaking the surface

islands.name: Grampus Rock
islands.note: Grampus: the old seamen's name for a blowing, spouting whale

islands.name: Porpoise Isle
islands.note: Porpoises play in its tide race

islands.name: Crab Cay
islands.note: Land crabs swarm its scrub at night

islands.name: Conch Cay
islands.note: Conch shells heaped on the beach

islands.name: Barracuda Cay
islands.note: Barracuda hang over its reef

islands.name: Bonefish Cay
islands.note: Bonefish tail on the flats around it

islands.name: Snapper Cay
islands.note: Good fishing for snapper off its edge

islands.name: Nurse Cay
islands.note: Nurse sharks sleep in its shallows; as in the Ragged Island Range

islands.name: Oyster Cay
islands.note: Mangrove oysters grow on its roots

islands.name: Crawfish Cay
islands.note: Crawfish: the Caribbean spiny lobster

islands.name: Mermaid's Purse Cay
islands.note: Mermaid's purse: the empty egg case of a skate, found on the tide line

islands.name: Devilfish Rock
islands.note: Devil-fish: the anglerfish, 'a hideous creature' (Smyth)

islands.name: Inkfish Rock
islands.note: Inkfish: the period name for squid and cuttlefish

islands.name: Flying Fish Cay
islands.note: Flying fish land on deck at night in these waters

islands.name: Sea Cow Island
islands.note: Sea cow: the sailors' name for the manatee grazing its seagrass

islands.name: Seahorse Cay
islands.note: Seahorses cling to its seagrass

islands.name: Grey Amber Cay
islands.note: Ambergris, 'grey amber', washed up from whales and was worth its weight in gold

islands.name: Whalebone Cay
islands.note: A whale's ribs bleach on its beach

islands.name: Sea Grape Cay
islands.note: Sea grape grows on sandy shores; its fruit makes a jam

islands.name: Coco Plum Cay
islands.note: Coco plum: a beach shrub with sweet fruit

islands.name: Mangrove Cay
islands.note: Mangroves standing in the water on their roots

islands.name: Lignum Vitae Cay
islands.note: Lignum vitae, ironwood: so dense it sinks; turned into sheaves for blocks

islands.name: Pumpion Cay
islands.note: Pumpion: the old word for pumpkin, kept on a cay off Andros

islands.name: Calabash Cay
islands.note: Calabash gourds served sailors as bowls and bailers

islands.name: Manchineel Cay
islands.note: The manchineel, 'little apple of death': fruit and sap burn; never shelter under it in rain

islands.name: Poisonwood Cay
islands.note: Poisonwood: brush against it and blister

islands.name: Samphire Rock
islands.note: Rock samphire, gathered from sea cliffs and pickled: 'half way down hangs one that gathers samphire' (King Lear)

islands.name: Thrift Holm
islands.note: Thrift, the sea pink, carpets its turf

islands.name: Garlic Holm
islands.note: After Ganinick in Scilly, Cornish for the place of wild garlic

islands.name: Elder Isle
islands.note: Tresco in Scilly is Cornish for the farm by the elder trees

islands.name: Scurvy Grass Holm
islands.note: Scurvy grass: the bitter cress sailors ate against scurvy

islands.name: Tamarind Isle
islands.note: Tamarind pods against scurvy and thirst

islands.name: Breadfruit Island
islands.note: The Bounty was carrying breadfruit plants when her crew mutinied

islands.name: Nutmeg Isle
islands.note: Spice islands were the richest landfall of the age

islands.name: Cinnamon Cay
islands.note: Cinnamon bark drying in the sun

islands.name: Clove Isle
islands.note: Cloves: once worth more than their weight in silver

islands.name: Pepper Cay
islands.note: Pepper grows wild in its thickets

islands.name: Ginger Cay
islands.note: As in the Bahamas' Ginger Cay

islands.name: Lime Cay
islands.note: Limes against scurvy; there is one off Port Royal in Jamaica

islands.name: Wild Orange Cay
islands.note: Sour oranges planted by early sailors went wild

islands.name: Plantain Isle
islands.note: Plantain walks gone back to bush

islands.name: Pineapple Cay
islands.note: After Eleuthera's Pineapple Cays

islands.name: Bamboo Cay
islands.note: Bamboo clacks in the wind

islands.name: Palmetto Cay
islands.note: Palmetto leaves for thatch and hats

islands.name: Lone Palm Cay
islands.note: One palm on a hump of sand: the castaway's island of every storybook

islands.name: Three Palms Cay
islands.note: Three palms make a mark to steer by

islands.name: Gulfweed Cay
islands.note: Gulfweed: the floating sargassum that piles on its windward beach

islands.name: Mastic Cay
islands.note: Mastic trees; as in the Bahamas

islands.name: Logwood Island
islands.note: Logwood was cut for dye by the Baymen of Honduras

islands.name: Mahogany Isle
islands.note: Mahogany, cut for captains' cabins

islands.name: Mast Island
islands.note: Tall straight pines fit for masts, the most valuable timber of the age

islands.name: Spar Island
islands.note: Timber for yards and booms

islands.name: Pitch Pine Island
islands.note: Pine tar and pitch for seams and rigging

islands.name: Cedar Isle
islands.note: Cedar for planking light boats

islands.name: Greenheart Island
islands.note: Greenheart: a timber so hard the shipworm leaves it alone

islands.name: Juniper Holm
islands.note: Juniper scrub on a grassy holm

islands.name: Driftwood Cay
islands.note: Bleached driftwood stacked by the gales

islands.name: Wrack Cay
islands.note: Wrack: weed and wreckage cast up by the sea

islands.name: Scrub Cay
islands.note: Nothing but scrub; as in the Bahamas

islands.name: Tear Coat Cay
islands.note: A Bahamian cay whose thorny scrub tears a coat to rags

islands.name: Turtle Grass Cay
islands.note: Meadows of turtle grass all round it

islands.name: Sugar Loaf Island
islands.note: A cone like a loaf of sugar; sugar loaf hills mark every period chart

islands.name: Cocked Hat Island
islands.note: Three-cornered like a tricorne; navigators also call the triangle of three crossed bearings a cocked hat

islands.name: Thrum Cap
islands.note: Cook's name in Dusky Sound for a knob like a sailor's woollen thrum cap

islands.name: Saddleback Island
islands.note: Two humps and a dip like a saddle

islands.name: Elbow Cay
islands.note: Bent like an elbow; Abaco and the Exumas both have one

islands.name: Table Island
islands.note: Flat-topped and steep-sided, like Cook's Table Cape

islands.name: Gable End Isle
islands.note: Cook: a white cliff like the gable end of a house

islands.name: Pigeon House Rock
islands.note: Cook: a peak shaped like the top of a dovecote

islands.name: Mitre Rock
islands.note: Split at the top like a bishop's mitre

islands.name: Steeple Rock
islands.note: A spire of rock seen from far off

islands.name: Chimney Stack
islands.note: Tall, square and smoking with spray

islands.name: Pulpit Rock
islands.note: A ledge like a preacher's pulpit

islands.name: Anvil Rock
islands.note: Flat-topped with a horn at one end

islands.name: Thimble Rock
islands.note: Small, round and pitted

islands.name: Kettle Rock
islands.note: Round as a kettle, and it boils when the sea runs

islands.name: Teapot Rock
islands.note: A spout, a handle and a lid, if you squint

islands.name: Coffin Island
islands.note: Long, flat and black

islands.name: Barrel of Butter
islands.note: The name sailors at Scapa Flow gave a rock there

islands.name: Plum Duff Cay
islands.note: Duff: the sailors' boiled pudding (Smyth); a round brown lump of a cay

islands.name: Hardtack Cay
islands.note: Flat, dry and hard as ship's biscuit

islands.name: Sea Pie Island
islands.note: Sea pie: the sailors' pie of meat and crust in layers

islands.name: Burgoo Isle
islands.note: Burgoo: seafaring porridge of boiled oatmeal (Smyth)

islands.name: Salmagundi Cay
islands.note: Salmagundi: the pirates' heaped salad of everything aboard

islands.name: Johnny Cake Cay
islands.note: Johnny cake: the fried bread of the islands

islands.name: Noah's Ark Island
islands.note: Long, with a high house amidships; Noah's ark is also the seamen's name for a long cloud foretelling weather

islands.name: Dutchman's Breeches
islands.note: Two legs and a waist; and the patch of blue in a breaking gale, 'enough to make a pair of breeches for a Dutchman' (Smyth)

islands.name: Old Wife Stack
islands.note: A bent stack like an old woman in a shawl

islands.name: Topsail Rock
islands.note: Looks like a sail on the horizon

islands.name: Stranger Sail
islands.note: A pale rock that every lookout calls as a sail at dusk

islands.name: Whale Rock
islands.note: Cook's name for a sunken rock the Endeavour struck

islands.name: Horseshoe Island
islands.note: Curved round a lagoon

islands.name: Sickle Cay
islands.note: A thin curve of sand

islands.name: Long Cay
islands.note: The plainest and commonest cay name of all

islands.name: Round Island
islands.note: Plain and round

islands.name: Flat Island
islands.note: Cook's plainest kind of name

islands.name: Woody Island
islands.note: Another of Cook's plain names

islands.name: Shipstern Cay
islands.note: High and square at one end like a ship's stern; as in Belize

islands.name: Capstan Isle
islands.note: Round and drum-shaped

islands.name: Ropewalk Island
islands.note: Long and straight as the shed where cables are laid up

islands.name: Monkey's Fist Rock
islands.note: Monkey's fist: the ball knot on the end of a heaving line

islands.name: Reef Knot Cay
islands.note: Two loops of reef tied together

islands.name: Bowline Island
islands.note: Looped round a lagoon like a bowline

islands.name: Sheepshank Cay
islands.note: Long and doubled back on itself

islands.name: Hawsehole Rock
islands.note: Pierced like the hole the anchor cable runs through

islands.name: Lubber's Hole
islands.note: Smyth: the gap timid climbers use to get into the top; here, an arch a boat can pass

islands.name: Needle's Eye
islands.note: An arch too narrow for anything bigger than a jolly boat

islands.name: Keyhole Rock
islands.note: An arch shaped like a keyhole

islands.name: Porthole Stack
islands.note: A round hole through a stack

islands.name: Bosun's Whistle
islands.note: The wind pipes through a hole in it like a boatswain's call

islands.name: Bellows Island
islands.note: A blowhole breathes spray with every swell

islands.name: Drum Rock
islands.note: The swell booms in its cave like a drum

islands.name: Echo Isle
islands.note: A cave that answers back

islands.name: Cave Holm
islands.note: After Orkney's Helliar Holm, the cave island

islands.name: Nobody Knows What
islands.note: Cook's name in Dusky Sound for an arm he had no time to explore

islands.name: Somebody Knows What
islands.note: Vancouver's answer, when he went back and explored Cook's Nobody Knows What

islands.name: Apparent Island
islands.note: A Cook name in Breaksea Sound; the island was not there

islands.name: Mistaken Isle
islands.note: Cook named Mistaken Bay for an inlet that turned out to be a valley

islands.name: Doubtless Cay
islands.note: Cook's Doubtless Bay: the wind kept him from looking inside

islands.name: Doubtful Island
islands.note: Cook would not risk Doubtful Harbour, not knowing if he could get out again

islands.name: Useless Island
islands.note: A Cook name; it was

islands.name: Luncheon Cay
islands.note: Cook's Luncheon Cove: where they ate lunch

islands.name: Supper Isle
islands.note: Cook's Supper Cove: where they ate dinner

islands.name: Sunday Isle
islands.note: Cook's Sunday Cove: visited on a Sunday

islands.name: Wet Jacket Island
islands.note: Cook's Wet Jacket Arm, where his officer was caught in a downpour

islands.name: Turnagain Island
islands.note: Cook's Cape Turnagain, where he met foul weather and turned back

islands.name: Farewell Island
islands.note: Cook's Cape Farewell, his last sight of New Zealand

islands.name: Foulwind Isle
islands.note: Cook's Cape Foulwind, after days of rain, squalls and gales

islands.name: Breaksea Island
islands.note: Cook's name for an island that shelters a sound from the swell

islands.name: Hope Cay
islands.note: Cook's Hope Islands, between his leaking ship and safety

islands.name: Tribulation Rock
islands.note: Cook's Cape Tribulation: 'here begun all our troubles'

islands.name: Weary Cay
islands.note: Cook's Weary Bay, named after the crew had pumped all night

islands.name: Poverty Island
islands.note: Cook's Poverty Bay 'afforded us no one thing we wanted'

islands.name: Plenty Island
islands.note: Cook's Bay of Plenty, named to answer Poverty Bay

islands.name: Disappointment Island
islands.note: There is one in the Auckland Islands, and a Disappointment Cove in Cook's Breaksea Sound

islands.name: Detention Isle
islands.note: Cook's Detention Cove

islands.name: Occasional Cay
islands.note: Cook's Occasional Cove

islands.name: Runaway Cay
islands.note: Cook's Cape Runaway

islands.name: Come-By-Chance Island
islands.note: A Newfoundland harbour, said to have been found by sailors by chance

islands.name: Seldom-Come-By
islands.note: An old Newfoundland outport name: a place few ships reach

islands.name: Heart's Content
islands.note: A Newfoundland harbour named in the age of sail

islands.name: Heart's Delight
islands.note: Newfoundland fishermen named harbours for what they hoped to find

islands.name: Heart's Desire
islands.note: Another Newfoundland harbour name

islands.name: Little Heart's Ease
islands.note: A Newfoundland name: rest after a hard passage

islands.name: Run-By-Guess
islands.note: A Newfoundland name: found by dead reckoning and luck

islands.name: Famish Isle
islands.note: After Newfoundland's Famish Gut

islands.name: Over Yonder Cay
islands.note: A real Exuma cay, named for lying across from a busier one

islands.name: Landfall Cay
islands.note: The first land sighted after a passage

islands.name: Twice Found Island
islands.note: Charted twice, by two crews who each thought it theirs

islands.name: Galley Packet Cay
islands.note: Galley-packet: sailors' slang for an unfounded rumour (Smyth)

islands.name: Second Thoughts Cay
islands.note: Where captains turn back

islands.name: Fair Chance Isle
islands.note: A fair wind and a fair chance

islands.name: Odd Shoe Cay
islands.note: One shoe on the tide line; nobody knows whose

islands.name: Lost Anchor Cay
islands.note: An anchor fouled on its reef and left there

islands.name: Broken Oar Cay
islands.note: Half an oar stuck upright in the sand

islands.name: Footprint Cay
islands.note: A single footprint in the sand, as Crusoe found

islands.name: Friday Cay
islands.note: After Crusoe's Friday, and the day it was charted

islands.name: Sandglass Cay
islands.note: Waisted like the glass that times the log line

islands.name: Eight Bells Island
islands.note: Eight bells: the end of a watch

islands.name: Dogwatch Cay
islands.note: The dog watches, four to eight in the evening, when the crew sings

islands.name: Middle Watch Rock
islands.note: The middle watch, midnight to four, the loneliest at sea

islands.name: Lubberland
islands.note: Lubber-land: 'a kind of El Dorado in sea-story, or country of pleasure without work' (Smyth)

islands.name: Fiddler's Green
islands.note: The sailors' paradise of folklore, where the fiddle never stops

islands.name: Davy Jones's Doorstep
islands.note: Davy Jones's locker is the bottom of the sea; this is the step before it

islands.name: Corposant Rock
islands.note: Corposant: St Elmo's fire, the pale light on mastheads in a storm

islands.name: Devil's Smile
islands.note: Devil's smiles: 'gleams of sunshine among dark clouds, either in the heavens or captain's face' (Smyth)

islands.name: Cat's Paw Cay
islands.note: Cat's-paw: a light air ruffling a calm

islands.name: Doldrum Cay
islands.note: The doldrums: 'those parts of the sea where calms are known to prevail' (Smyth)

islands.name: Dutchman's Rock
islands.note: Some say the Flying Dutchman was last seen rounding it

islands.name: Old Scratch Rock
islands.note: Old Scratch: a sailors' name for the Devil, as Old Harry is on the Dorset stack

islands.name: Bumbo Isle
islands.note: Bumbo: rum, water, sugar and nutmeg

islands.name: Rumbullion Cay
islands.note: Rumbullion: the first name for rum, in Barbados in the 1650s

islands.name: Kill-Devil Cay
islands.note: Kill-devil: another early name for rough rum

islands.name: Grog Blossom Isle
islands.note: Grog-blossom: the red nose of a hard drinker (Smyth); for its red cliffs

islands.name: Sixpence Cay
islands.note: After the Bahamas' Six Shilling Cay, named for coins washed ashore

islands.name: Ha'penny Rock
islands.note: Hardly worth landing on

islands.name: Doubloon Cay
islands.note: A gold doubloon turned up in its sand

islands.name: Moidore Cay
islands.note: Moidore: the Portuguese gold coin common in the West Indies

islands.name: Pistole Isle
islands.note: Pistole: the Spanish gold double escudo

islands.name: Lost Ring Cay
islands.note: After the Exumas' Gold Ring Cay, named for something found on the beach

islands.name: Glass Cay
islands.note: Bahamian name for a cay strewn with glass from a wreck; or black volcanic glass

islands.name: Bottle Cay
islands.note: Where the current lands bottles, and the messages in them

islands.name: Sea Chest Cay
islands.note: A sailor's sea chest washed up here, empty

islands.name: Silver Spoon Cay
islands.note: Somebody's silver spoon, and no one to claim it

islands.name: Copper-Bottom Cay
islands.note: Copper-bottomed: sound and trustworthy, like a sheathed hull

islands.name: Wrecker's Cay
islands.note: Bahamian wreckers lived by salvaging ships lost on the reefs

islands.name: Salvage Cay
islands.note: Timbers from a wreck stacked above the tide line

islands.name: Lagan Rocks
islands.note: Lagan: goods sunk with a buoy to mark them, to be claimed later

islands.name: Derelict Isle
islands.note: An abandoned hull lies on its beach

islands.name: Shroud Cay
islands.note: Bahamian: probably for burials at sea, sewn in a shroud of sailcloth

islands.name: Careening Cay
islands.note: Ships were hove down on such beaches to clean their hulls; Jamaica's Port Royal was Careening Cay before the English renamed it

islands.name: Ballast Cay
islands.note: Ships took on sand and stone here for ballast

islands.name: Ironbound Isle
islands.note: Ironbound: a coast of cliffs with no landing

islands.name: Weatherbound Island
islands.note: Where ships wait out the wind

islands.name: Halfway Rock
islands.note: Halfway from port to the rim

islands.name: Danger Cay
islands.note: As in the Exumas, for the shoals off it

islands.name: Mind Yourselves Rocks
islands.note: English for Mira Por Vos, Bahamian rocks whose Spanish name means 'watch out for yourselves'

islands.name: Sleepless Cay
islands.note: After Quita Sueño, 'takes away sleep', a Caribbean reef that kept pilots awake

islands.name: Snoring Cay
islands.note: After Roncador, 'the snorer', a Caribbean cay named for its roaring surf

islands.name: Eyes-Open Rocks
islands.note: After the Abrolhos, which sailors read as abre olhos, 'open your eyes'

islands.name: Breakers Cay
islands.note: Surf breaks on it in any swell

islands.name: Grumbling Rocks
islands.note: The surf grumbles in their gullies

islands.name: Growler Rock
islands.note: A low rock that growls in the swell

islands.name: Hellweathers
islands.note: A reef in the Isles of Scilly; the name says enough

islands.name: Overfall Rock
islands.note: Overfalls: broken water where a current pours over a ledge

islands.name: Roaring Water Rocks
islands.note: Breakers you hear long before you see them

islands.name: Fathom Rock
islands.note: One fathom over it at best

islands.name: Sounding Cay
islands.note: Where the lead goes down every few boat lengths

islands.name: Spindrift Isle
islands.note: Spindrift: spray blown off the crests, drifting like smoke

islands.name: Brume Holm
islands.note: Brume: sea mist

islands.name: Haar Holm
islands.note: Haar: the cold sea fog of the north

islands.name: Spume Rock
islands.note: Wet with flying spume in any wind

islands.name: Loom Isle
islands.note: Loom: 'an indistinct enlarged appearance of any distant object' (Smyth)

islands.name: Blink Rock
islands.note: Blink: a brightness in the sky over distant ice or land (Smyth)

islands.name: Ne Plus Ultra
islands.note: 'Nothing further beyond': the warning said to be carved on the Pillars of Hercules

islands.name: Hindmost Isle
islands.note: The last island before the falls

islands.name: Outermost Holm
islands.note: Nothing lies beyond it but mist

islands.name: Last Sight Cay
islands.note: The last land a boat sees before the falls

islands.name: World's End Skerry
islands.note: So it is

islands.name: Lip Stack
islands.note: So near the lip that spray from the falls drifts over it

islands.name: Thunder Holm
islands.note: The falls can be heard from it on a still night

islands.name: Hy-Brasil
islands.note: Irish phantom island, on charts from 1325 to the 1860s, said to show through the mist once every seven years

islands.name: Antillia
islands.note: The island of seven cities of Iberian legend, on 15th-century charts

islands.name: Royllo
islands.note: A phantom island drawn west of Antillia in 1424

islands.name: Mayda
islands.note: A crescent-shaped phantom island that stayed on charts for centuries

islands.name: Buss Island
islands.note: Reported in 1578 near Greenland and never found again

islands.name: Pepys Island
islands.note: Reported in 1683 and named for Samuel Pepys; never found

islands.name: Saxemberg Island
islands.note: Reported in 1670 in the South Atlantic; searched for and never found

islands.name: Bermeja
islands.note: A Spanish island off Yucatán that vanished from the charts

islands.name: Isle of Demons
islands.note: A haunted island off Newfoundland on 16th-century maps

islands.name: Saint Brendan's Isle
islands.note: Said to have been landed on by a monk in 512, and to drift away from ships that approach

islands.name: Frisland
islands.note: A phantom island of the Zeno map

islands.name: Lyonesse
islands.note: The drowned land of Cornish legend between Land's End and Scilly

islands.name: Isle of Ys
islands.note: The drowned city of Breton legend, whose bells ring under the sea

islands.name: Thule Rock
islands.note: Thule: the farthest land the ancients knew; ultima Thule, the end of the world

islands.name: Fata Morgana
islands.note: The mirage that lifts islands into the sky

islands.name: Lodestone Island
islands.note: Legend put a black magnetic rock at the pole that drew the nails out of ships

islands.name: Muckle Holm
islands.note: Muckle: big (Scots and Shetland)

islands.name: Peerie Holm
islands.note: Peerie: small (Shetland)

islands.name: Outskerry
islands.note: After the Out Skerries, the outermost rocks of Shetland

islands.name: Auk Skerry
islands.note: Auks nest in its cracks

islands.name: Finfolk Skerry
islands.note: Orkney's finfolk: sea people who row without oars

islands.name: Trow Holm
islands.note: Trows: the trolls of Shetland, who come out at dusk

islands.name: Simmer Dim Isle
islands.note: Simmer dim: the Shetland midsummer twilight that never goes dark

islands.name: Clett Rock
islands.note: Clett: 'a rock broken from a cliff' (Smyth)

islands.name: The Calf
islands.note: Calf: an islet off a larger island, as a calf beside a cow, like the Calf of Man (Smyth)

islands.name: Holystone Island
islands.note: Holystone: the sandstone sailors scrubbed the decks with on their knees

islands.name: Grindstone Island
islands.note: Round, grey and gritty

islands.name: Whetstone Rock
islands.note: Long and grey; good for an edge

islands.name: Millstone Rock
islands.note: Round and flat

islands.name: Grey Mare Rock
islands.note: A grey hump like a horse's back

islands.name: Clinker Island
islands.note: Clinker: the fused lumps from a furnace; also a boat whose planks overlap

islands.name: The Forge
islands.note: It glows at night like a smith's forge

islands.name: Hearth Island
islands.note: Warm ground and steam: a hearth for cold sailors

islands.name: Cauldron Isle
islands.note: A crater with a boiling pool

islands.name: Tinderbox Island
islands.note: Dry as tinder

islands.name: Smoky Island
islands.note: Steam drifts from its vents

islands.name: Old Smoky
islands.note: A peak that has been smoking as long as anyone remembers

islands.name: Smouldering Isle
islands.note: Its fires never quite go out

islands.name: Pumice Cay
islands.note: Pumice: the rock that floats

islands.name: Burnt Island
islands.note: A common chart name for scorched ground

islands.name: Tumbledown Isle
islands.note: Rubble heaped like a fallen city, as on Fallen Jerusalem in the Virgin Islands

islands.name: Devil's Kitchen
islands.note: Steam and sulphur where the Devil cooks

islands.name: Firebrand Isle
islands.note: A red peak like a brand from the fire

islands.name: Furnace Island
islands.note: It roars and glows

islands.name: Sulphur Cay
islands.note: Yellow crusts round its vents

islands.name: Greenwood Isle
islands.note: Shade and green leaves after a long passage

islands.name: Gloaming Isle
islands.note: Gloaming: dusk; its woods are dark by mid-afternoon

islands.name: Sweetwater Cay
islands.note: Fresh water on a small cay was worth marking on a chart

islands.name: Cistern Cay
islands.note: Bahamian: rainwater pools in its rock

islands.name: Well Cay
islands.note: A well dug by some earlier crew

islands.name: Cascade Isle
islands.note: Cook's Cascade Point: red cliffs with streams falling down them

islands.name: Spout Island
islands.note: Las Chorreras, 'the spouts', the Spanish name for Jamaica's falls at Ocho Rios

islands.name: Las Chorreras
islands.note: Spanish: the spouts; the falls at Ocho Rios, before the English garbled the name

islands.name: Weeping Rock
islands.note: Water seeps down its face in strings

islands.name: Blue Hole Cay
islands.note: A round deep pool, blue-black in the shallows

islands.name: Punchbowl Island
islands.note: A ring of land round a lagoon like a punch bowl

islands.name: Teacup Cay
islands.note: A ring of sand round a lagoon you could stir

islands.name: Jewel Box Isle
islands.note: Coral in every colour in its lagoon

islands.name: Beacon Cay
islands.note: Bahamian: for a beacon once kept to warn ships

islands.name: Watchfire Isle
islands.note: The stones of an old watchfire on its summit

islands.name: Old Signal Isle
islands.note: A ruined signal station on its top

islands.name: Chapel Cay
islands.note: A roofless chapel of coral stone

islands.name: Green Flash Cay
islands.note: Watch the sun set from it for the green flash

islands.name: Moonrise Isle
islands.note: The moon comes up behind it from the harbour

islands.name: Bella Stella Isle
islands.note: Bella stella: 'a name used by old seamen for the cross-staff' (Smyth)

islands.name: Lodestar Rock
islands.note: Lodestar: the star a ship steers by

islands.name: Reckoning Cay
islands.note: Where a navigator checks the dead reckoning

islands.name: Telltale Cay
islands.note: Telltales: the wool strips on a sail that show the wind

islands.name: Trade Wind Cay
islands.note: Always a breeze

islands.name: Lee Cay
islands.note: In the lee of a larger island

islands.name: Weather Isle
islands.note: On the weather side, taking the wind first

islands.name: Squall Rock
islands.note: Squalls come off it without warning

islands.name: Whitecap Cay
islands.note: White water all round it in a breeze

islands.name: Gale Holm
islands.note: It always seems to be blowing there

islands.name: Rat Cay
islands.note: Rats come ashore from ships; the Exumas have two

islands.name: Goat Island
islands.note: Goats were left on islands as food for passing ships

islands.name: Hog Island
islands.note: Pigs left to forage gave the Bahamas many Hog Cays, and Bermuda its wild hogs

islands.name: Iguana Cay
islands.note: Iguanas sun on its rocks; Guana Cay in the Bahamas

islands.name: Widow's Cay
islands.note: Nobody remembers whose widow

islands.name: Old Moll's Holm
islands.note: The tale says an old woman kept goats on it

islands.name: Granny Pell's Cay
islands.note: Named for someone's grandmother, like many a Bahamian cay

islands.name: Jack Straw's Island
islands.note: Jack Straw: a man of straw, a nobody

islands.name: Tom Tiddler's Island
islands.note: Tom Tiddler's ground: the old children's game of snatching gold and silver from the giant's patch

islands.name: Jolly Boat Cay
islands.note: Where every beginner first lands

islands.name: Bosun's Cay
islands.note: Where the boatswain sends the idlers to cut wood

islands.name: Sailmaker's Isle
islands.note: Flat ground to spread canvas on

islands.name: Shipwright's Isle
islands.note: Timber and a sloping beach to build on

islands.name: Cabin Boy Cay
islands.note: Small enough to be the cabin boy's

islands.name: Topman's Rock
islands.note: Only a topman could climb it

islands.name: Purser's Cay
islands.note: Smaller than it looks on the chart, like a purser's ration

islands.name: Cayo Perdido
islands.note: Spanish: the lost cay

islands.name: Isla Sola
islands.note: Spanish: the lonely island

islands.name: Cayo Ciego
islands.note: Spanish: the blind cay; low and hard to see

islands.name: Cayo Ventoso
islands.note: Spanish: the windy cay

islands.name: Isla del Humo
islands.note: Spanish: island of smoke

islands.name: Cayo Arena
islands.note: Spanish: sand cay; Columbus called the Ragged Islands the Islas de Arena

islands.name: Îlet Perdu
islands.note: French: the lost islet

islands.name: Îlet Fortune
islands.note: French: islet of luck; there is one off Guadeloupe

islands.name: Îlet Brûlé
islands.note: French: the burnt islet

islands.name: La Désirée
islands.note: French: the longed-for one; Columbus's men named La Désirade for the land they longed to see

islands.name: Ilha Escondida
islands.note: Portuguese: the hidden island

islands.name: Broad Island
islands.note: Bressay in Shetland is Old Norse for the broad island

islands.name: Horse Island
islands.note: Hrossey, the Norse name for the Orkney Mainland, means horse island

islands.name: Grande Terre
islands.note: French: the great land, as Guadeloupe's eastern island

islands.name: Isla Grande
islands.note: Spanish: the big island, a name on many Spanish charts

islands.name: Thousand Palms Island
islands.note: More palms than anyone has counted

islands.name: Hollow Mountain Island
islands.note: A broken crater with the sea let in on one side

islands.name: Greatwood Island
islands.note: Forest from shore to summit

islands.name: Long Reach Island
islands.note: Long enough to sail a reach down its whole side

islands.name: Breakwind Island
islands.note: It stinks of sulphur, and the wind always seems to come from it

islands.name: Rotten Egg Cay
islands.note: Sulphur vents; smelt long before it is seen

islands.name: Bumboat Cay
islands.note: Bum-boat: 'a boat employed to carry provisions, vegetables, and small merchandise for sale to ships' (Smyth); the name is from bombard, a beer vessel

islands.name: Pooped Rock
islands.note: Pooped: when 'a heavy sea breaks over the stern' of a boat running before a gale, 'extremely dangerous' (Smyth)

islands.name: Seer's Rock
islands.note: In Highland and island lore a seer had the second sight, and could foresee who would drown before the boat sailed

groups.name: Hen and Chickens
groups.note: One big rock and a brood of small ones; Cook named a group so in 1769, and charts have many more

groups.name: The Aldermen
groups.note: Cook thought they looked like the Court of Aldermen in session

groups.name: Lookers-On
groups.note: Cook's name for onlookers who kept their distance

groups.name: The Paternosters
groups.note: Jersey's reef, where passing sailors said the Lord's Prayer for those wrecked there

groups.name: Parson and Clerk
groups.note: A tall rock and a short one, after a pair on the Devon coast

groups.name: The Brothers
groups.note: A common chart name for rocks of a size

groups.name: The Sisters
groups.note: A common chart name for islets of a size

groups.name: The Twins
groups.note: Bimini is said to be Lucayan for the twins

groups.name: Seven Sleepers
groups.note: Seven low islets that never stir

groups.name: The Snares
groups.note: Vancouver's name for a group he judged a hazard to shipping

groups.name: The Traps
groups.note: Cook: rock ledges that could catch unwary ships

groups.name: The Snorers
groups.note: Roncadores: Spanish for the reefs that roar

groups.name: The Doldrums
groups.note: Cays in calm water where nothing ever blows

groups.name: Five Fingers
groups.note: Cook: five high rocks like a hand

groups.name: The Tin Isles
groups.note: The Cassiterides: the ancients' tin islands, never certainly found

groups.name: Aurora Isles
groups.note: Phantom islands reported by a Spanish ship in 1762 and never seen again

groups.name: Sow and Pigs
groups.note: A chart name for a big rock and a litter of small ones

groups.name: Cow and Calves
groups.note: A big rock with calves beside it

groups.name: Mare and Foals
groups.note: A big island trailed by small ones

groups.name: Goose and Goslings
groups.note: Low cays in a line behind a bigger one

groups.name: Bread and Butter Cays
groups.note: After a pair of cays in Belize

groups.name: Pieces of Eight
groups.note: Eight cays, one for each real in a Spanish dollar

groups.name: The Ninepins
groups.note: Nine upright rocks, like Hong Kong's Ninepin Group

groups.name: The Skittles
groups.note: Short round stacks standing in a cluster

groups.name: Ducks and Drakes
groups.note: In a line like a stone skipped across water

groups.name: Stepping Stones
groups.note: A string of islets you could almost walk

groups.name: The Chessmen
groups.note: Stacks like chessmen on a board

groups.name: The Gossips
groups.note: The surf chatters among them day and night

groups.name: The Jury
groups.note: Twelve rocks, all of one mind

groups.name: Hare and Hounds
groups.note: One cay ahead and the rest strung out after it

groups.name: The Mourners
groups.note: Dark rocks bowed toward the falls

groups.name: The Whelps
groups.note: Whelps: small rocks around a big one, as the ribs round a capstan

groups.name: The Choir
groups.note: The wind sings in the gaps between them

groups.name: The Fiddlers
groups.note: Islets that seem to dance in the shimmer

groups.name: The Admirals
groups.note: Big, grey and immovable

groups.name: The Bellringers
groups.note: The surf booms in their caves like bells

groups.name: Peas in a Pod
groups.note: Small round cays all alike

groups.name: Three Graces
groups.note: Three fair islands side by side

groups.name: The Hogsheads
groups.note: Round as barrels

groups.name: The Pilgrims
groups.note: In single file across the sea

groups.name: Sea Wolves
groups.note: Rocks that lie in wait
